meta.title: Punctuation Power: The Starbase Code
meta.unit: Punctuation and grammar — full stops, commas, apostrophes, sentence types, capital letters
meta.subject: English: Language & Literature
meta.author: ISH English

story.intro: Captain, our ship is drifting! Five glowing star-stations float around us, each one locked by a puzzle about punctuation and grammar. Solve each station to win a glowing letter, then beam the secret word into the airlock to start the engines for home.
story.outro: The engines roar to life and the stars streak past — you punched in the code and saved the ship! You mastered the marks that keep our sentences clear, and that knowledge powered you all the way home.

finalCode.label: Spell the grammar treasure word from your letters

stations.name: The Mark That Doesn't Fit
stations.narrative: A space-station panel shows four punctuation marks. One of them is NOT a punctuation mark at all. Tap the odd one out to power up the panel.

content.prompt: Three of these are punctuation marks. Which word does NOT belong with the others?

hints: Three of these are tiny marks you write in a sentence.
A full stop, a comma and a question mark are all punctuation.
The odd one is a TYPE OF WORD, not a mark — it is a doing word.
stations.reveal: Correct — a 'verb' is a doing word, not a punctuation mark. The other three are all punctuation! You win the glowing letter: N.

stations.name: The Missing Apostrophe
stations.narrative: A floating sign has lost a tiny mark. One word is missing its apostrophe. Type the word the way it should look.

content.text: The little robot waved at us. 'Hello! ____ so happy to meet you,' it beeped.

hints: The robot is joining two words: 'I' and 'am'.
An apostrophe takes the place of the missing letter 'a'.
Write 'I' then an apostrophe then 'm' — I'm.
stations.reveal: Yes — 'I'm' is short for 'I am', and the apostrophe replaces the missing 'a'. You win the glowing letter: O.

stations.name: The Sentence Scanner
stations.narrative: The ship's scanner reads a sentence and asks you one question about it. Choose the right answer to unlock the scanner.

content.passage: The astronaut floated to the window. Outside, the planet glowed a deep blue. 'Wow, look at that!' she gasped with a huge smile.
content.question: What type of sentence is 'Wow, look at that!' ?
options: a statement that just gives a fact
an exclamation that shows strong feeling
a question that asks for an answer
a command that is calm and quiet

stations.answer: an exclamation that shows strong feeling
acceptedAnswers: an exclamation that shows strong feeling
hints: Look at the mark at the end of the sentence — it is an exclamation mark!
An exclamation shows a big feeling, like surprise or excitement.
She is amazed and excited — pick the option about strong feeling.
stations.reveal: Right — it ends with an exclamation mark (!) and shows strong feeling, so it is an exclamation. You win the glowing letter: U.

stations.name: The Name-Word Vault
stations.narrative: An alien guard asks you to name the kind of word it protects. Read the clue and type the grammar word.

content.definition: A naming word: a word for a person, place, animal or thing — like 'planet', 'captain' or 'rocket'.
content.sentence: 'Comet' and 'galaxy' are both this kind of word: a ____.

hints: It is the kind of word that names a person, place or thing.
'Dog', 'school' and 'Mars' are all examples of it.
It begins with 'n' and rhymes with 'down' — a ____.
stations.reveal: Yes — a 'noun' is a naming word for a person, place, animal or thing. You win the glowing letter: N.

stations.name: The Scrambled Star-Mark
stations.narrative: The final star-mark has shattered into jumbled letters. Unscramble them to name the pause-mark and launch for home.

content.clue: The little curved mark you use to separate items in a list, like apples, pears and plums.

hints: It is a tiny curved mark that makes you pause for a moment.
You use it between items in a list: 'red, blue and green'.
Five letters, begins with 'c' — re-arrange them to spell COMMA.
stations.reveal: COMMA — the mark that separates items and gives a short pause. You win the final glowing letter: S.
